headline: Transmission models carry incomplete data, spatial transport and network topology
label: Transmission Modeling Under Incomplete Data
summary: Agent-based, PDE and network models now treat incomplete observation and contact structure as dynamical components rather than fixed inputs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that transmission models are being built around the observation process or host contact structure rather than fixed, complete inputs. An agent-based study of South Korean metro areas finds contact-tracing effectiveness collapses beyond city-specific omission thresholds, about 4% in Seoul. A chemotaxis-inspired PDE model of airborne infectious disease introduces a spatially-aware reproduction number with stabilized numerics, tested on Lombardy and Georgia simulations. A replicator SIS model on host networks shows heterogeneity speeds multi-strain coinfection dynamics while reducing strain coexistence. A Bayesian recursive filter estimating temperature-dependent Rt outperforms fixed-interval estimators on simulated and Singapore dengue data. What is new relative to fixed-parameter approaches is that incomplete observation, spatial transport, and network topology are carried explicitly into the dynamics rather than absorbed into inputs. A reporting standard, MIReVTD, targets findability and reuse of vector trait data in vector-borne disease modelling.
